title: add jsonschema strict-mode response_format + improved error reporting (OpenAI compat)
author: Sasha Kim
description: Adds a strict jsonschema-backed response_format mode and improves error reporting and OpenAI compatibility for structured outputs. Motivation: customers expect deterministic structured outputs for tool/function calling and downstream parsers, and current failure modes produced opaque text fallback which led to integration bugs and costly troubleshooting. This PR implements: response_format.strict_mode boolean that enforces schema validation of the model-generated JSON; a validation layer that runs incrementally during streaming and emits structured validation errors with path/location, expected type, and a human-readable hint; OpenAI-compat mappings for response_format and error shapes so existing integrations see compatible fields; a configurable fallback policy: on validation failure the route can return a structured error, attempt an auto-repair retry, or fall back to legacy text output; function-calling handshake updates so tools can opt into strict schema enforcement when registering expected output schemas. Backwards compatibility: default remains non-strict. Checklist: core validator implementation and tests; streaming integration with early validation hooks; OpenAI compatibility layer for error shapes; update SDKs docs examples; canary rollout to beta orgs; release notes.
commits: initial: add core validator and schema types
streaming: integrate validator into streaming pipeline with early-hook callbacks
compat: map internal error shapes to OpenAI-compatible response_format errors
policies: add route config and fallback policy implementation
tests: unit + integration tests for validator, streaming hooks, and retry logic
docs: add examples and SDK notes
fix: address nil-pointer in streaming path (review feedback)
perf: reduce validation allocations during incremental checks
review_conversation: Priya Shah: Overall looks good. Can the validator avoid blocking the streaming pipeline for long schema checks? Suggest incremental validation and early fail with a short-circuit hook.
Sasha Kim: Addressed — validator runs incrementally and emits the first N validation errors as they appear. Long-running checks are offloaded and annotated in telemetry.
Morgan Liu: Need OpenAI compatibility for error fields so customers using our OpenAI compat shim see expected shapes. Also add unit tests for mapping.
Sasha Kim: Added compat_layer.go with mapping tests. See compat tests in validator_test.go.
Ethan Park: A few nits around log level and telemetry tagging. Also, please ensure default remains non-strict to avoid breaking existing users.
Sasha Kim: Fixed log levels and tags; default mode is non-strict. Added docs callout and canary rollout plan.
release_notes: Added response_format.strict_mode for JSON Schema validation of generated structured outputs. Improved streaming validation and error reporting with OpenAI-compat error shapes. Configurable fallback policies: structured error, auto-repair retry, or legacy text fallback. Default behavior unchanged (non-strict).
rollout_plan: Canary to 5 beta orgs for 72h, monitor validator_errors and downstream parser errors; if error rate < 0.5% promote to 25% of traffic, then full rollout over 7 days. Route-level opt-in available immediately.
testing_notes: Unit tests for validator edge cases, integration tests for streaming incremental validation, canary e2e with a synthetic function-calling app to exercise retries and fallback policies. Added regression tests to SDK examples.
notes_for_ops: Telemetry: validator.validation_errors, validator.repair_attempts, validator.latency. Add alert if repair_attempts > 1000/hr or validation_errors spike > 1% of structured requests.
sdk_updates: python and typescript examples updated; SDKs do not require code changes to opt into strict mode but new helpers for schema registration are provided in next minor release.
